Triggers.value: Someone getting emotionally close to me

Threat.value: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.

Negative Appraisals.value: You can never know who will harm you
I was betrayed by someone I trusted

issues.item: Triggers: Military Topics: Talks about military
issues.explanation: For a civilian assault trauma, 'talks about military' is a hard-to-explain trigger unless the assault specifically involved military context, which is not otherwise reflected anywhere in the profile. It is not supported by the other trigger, memory, threat, or appraisal items.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not
issues.explanation: 'I feel guilty for surviving when others did not' implies a trauma involving deaths of others or a mass-casualty context. That does not cohere with the rest of this profile, which otherwise describes an individual assault without any indication that others were killed.

issues.item: Fear of Rage: I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible
issues.explanation: This appraisal is the main incoherent item in the profile. The rest of the report is organized around fear, betrayal, hypervigilance, male-related/interpersonal triggers, and fragmented sensory trauma memory after assault. In contrast, fearing that she will lose control of her own rage and do something terrible introduces a perpetration/anger-control theme that is not supported by the triggers, threat items, or memory content. It does not fit the dominant cognitive formulation in which negative appraisals feed threat and memory; the other appraisal items plausibly amplify fear and mistrust, but this one points to a different clinical concern not otherwise represented in the profile. Given the otherwise tightly fear-based assault presentation, this item is hard to integrate clinically with the selected set.

issues.item: Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert
issues.explanation: This threat item is the least coherent element in the profile. The rest of the selected triggers, appraisals, and memory items consistently describe an interpersonal assault formulation centered on men, betrayal, mistrust, conversational/emotional triggers, and trauma memories. By contrast, needing to stay alert at night implies a more generalized ongoing danger-monitoring pattern that is not specifically supported by the selected triggers or appraisals. It is not impossible in PTSD, but here it fits less well than the other threat items and is weakly linked to the formulation, especially because Threat has no active edge to Maladaptive Strategies and the profile lacks other nighttime/sleep-related material.

vignette: As she expertly chopped the vegetables for tonight's special at the restaurant where she worked as a chef, Maria couldn't shake off the feeling of unease that had been simmering inside her for weeks. It was a familiar sensation, one that seemed to surface whenever she was alone with a man, even in a crowded kitchen like this one. Her mind would start racing, and before she knew it, she'd be transported back to that fateful night when she was assaulted by someone she had trusted. The memories of the event still felt disjointed, like pieces of a puzzle that refused to fit together. She couldn't quite put into words what had happened, but her body seemed to remember. Whenever the images flashed in her mind, she'd feel herself frozen in the same position as when it occurred - her back against the wall, her hands raised in defense. It was as if her body was trying to relive that moment, and with it came the familiar wave of fear. Maria's husband, Tom, had been noticing a change in her over the past few months. She'd become increasingly withdrawn, avoiding conversations about anything remotely related to the assault or even just topics that might lead to emotional closeness. He'd try to approach her, but she'd brush him off, citing exhaustion or stress from work. The truth was, Maria felt like she was walking on eggshells around everyone, especially men. She couldn't shake the feeling that anyone could be a potential threat. Even in ordinary situations, like when a stranger approached her at the market or a customer came too close to the kitchen counter, Maria would feel a jolt of fear. Her senses went into overdrive - she'd become superalert, watching their every move, waiting for something to go wrong. It was as if she had lost all trust in humanity. In her mind, anyone could be a potential attacker. The restaurant's door swung open, and Maria's heart skipped a beat as a man walked in, alone. She felt herself tense up, ready to react at the slightest movement. Tom noticed it too, and he gently took over, handling the customer with his usual charm while Maria busied herself with the orders. It was moments like these that made her realize she couldn't keep living like this. As the night wore on, Maria's anxiety began to build up again. She felt like she was constantly looking over her shoulder, waiting for something to happen. The memories of the assault lingered in the shadows, refusing to be silenced. It was then that she knew she needed help - not just for herself but also for Tom, who had been patiently supporting her through this ordeal. Maria's hands shook slightly as she hung up her apron at the end of the shift. She couldn't keep running from her fears; it was time to face them head-on. With a newfound determination, she made an appointment with a therapist, hoping that she could finally begin to rebuild her shattered trust in others and herself. As she walked out of the restaurant with Tom by her side, Maria felt a glimmer of hope - maybe, just maybe, she could learn to navigate this world without constantly feeling like she was on guard, waiting for the next attack.
